When trying to lose weight, why not just eat at the BMR calories of your target weight?

When you have a flat tire, why don't you just replace it with a working tire?

Answer: Not everyone knows how or where to learn.

Counting calories is always a long numbers game. If you adjust either later in the day or the next day you can still hit your calories. Hell, a Coke is 100 calories add a handful of Pringles and that's another 100. That's 200 calories that could easily be cut. As long as you take in less calories over long periods of time you lose weight. One day doesn't make or break your diet.

There are a variety of reasons, the obeast in question may be in an urgent medical situation and rapid weightloss may be required. If you eat your target weight BMR calories then, as you approach your target, your weight loss will slow. Eating at a 500 to 1000 calorie a day defecit will consistently get 1 to 2 lbs a week of weight loss. It's encouraging, when losing weight, to see consistent results, imagine how frustrating it would be to take months to lose that last 5 or 10 lbs.

There are a ton of biological processes that go into functioning as a human being. Your brain function, energy levels, hormone levels, immune system function and countless bodily processes all depend on having enough energy for your cells to carry out their jobs. Yes, they'll start using fat instead of the food you're supposed to be eating to survive, but that is bare minimum survival we're talking about and it's not healthy or optimal.

So basically, cutting 500 kcals from your BMR in your diet per day is the go-to advice because it's very manageable to do, increases likelihood of compliance because it doesn't make you feel like complete and total dog-shit, and allows you to continue to be healthy while you lose weight.
